title: Microsoft Teams: Security detections report in the Teams admin center
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, report details, admin paths and protection command are supported by Microsoft's documentation. It correctly distinguishes product-level Teams licensing from unpublished report-specific requirements and leaves the report's default state unstated.

claims.quote: A new Security Detection Report in the Teams admin center provides a centralized view of messaging security detections

claims.where: controls[0].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The report is reached in Teams admin center at Analytics & reports > Protection reports > View reports > Report > Security detections.
claims.quote: In the left navigation of the Teams admin center, go to Analytics & reports > Protection reports. On the View reports tab, under Report, select Security detections.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table and prose
claims.claim: No PowerShell or Microsoft Graph operation is documented for viewing or exporting this report as of November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/graph "Teams" "security detections report"; site:learn.microsoft.com/powershell/module/microsoftteams "security detections report". Read security-detections-report, teams-reporting-reference and Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration; no report operation found.

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: File protection is configured in Teams admin center at Messaging settings > Messaging safety > Scan messages for file types that are not allowed.
claims.quote: In the left navigation, select Messaging settings. Scroll down to Messaging safety settings. Turn on the setting: Scan messages for file types that are not allowed.

claims.claim: Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -FileTypeCheck "Enabled" -Identity Global enables file protection using the Teams PowerShell module.
claims.quote: You can also configure file protection using PowerShell with the Teams module: Set-CsTeamsMessagingConfiguration -FileTypeCheck "Enabled" -Identity Global

claims.claim: Weaponizable File Protection blocks messages containing listed file types in chats and channels.
claims.quote: Enhanced security protection in Microsoft Teams automatically blocks messages containing potentially weaponizable file types in chats and channels.

claims.claim: Weaponizable File Protection is a tenant-wide setting.
claims.quote: Once enabled, all users in the tenant will have file protection applied to their Teams messages.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: The Weaponizable File Protection row configures the protection rather than the Security detections report.
claims.quote: -FileTypeCheck ... This setting enables weaponizable file detection in Teams messages in the tenant.

claims.claim: The file protection feature page says its blocked file-type list is not configurable.
claims.quote: The list of blocked file types isn't currently configurable by administrators.

claims.claim: The PowerShell reference documents CustomBlockList with FileTypeBlockList when FileTypeCheck is Enabled.
claims.quote: This setting applies only when FileTypeCheck is set to Enabled. This setting applies only when FileTypeCustomizationSetting is set to CustomBlockList.

claims.where: Open questions; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: The report page gives Last 7 days and Last 30 days as examples of predefined date ranges.
claims.quote: Under Date range, select a predefined time range. For example, Last 7 days or Last 30 days.

claims.claim: The maximum report lookback and detection-record retention period are not published for this report.
claims.quote: Searched: "Security detections report" retention date range maximum. Read security-detections-report and teams-reporting-reference; neither gives a maximum lookback or retention period. Defender for Office 365 retention results concern a different reporting product.

claims.claim: The reporting reference's concealment note names the Teams user activity, device usage and usage reports.
claims.quote: Enabling this setting de-identifies user, group, and site name information in the Teams user activity report, Teams device usage report, and Teams usage report.

claims.claim: Whether usage-report name concealment also applies to the Security detections report remains unconfirmed.
claims.quote: Searched: "Security detections report" conceal anonymous "FileTypeCheck". Read security-detections-report and teams-reporting-reference: concealment is described for usage reports and three named Teams reports, not clearly for this security report.
